**same `docid`** whenever they denote the same underlying legal authority, even if their wording differs.\n\nUse all available evidence, including:\n\n* titles\n* citations\n* abbreviations\n* Determine which legal authority the mention refers to.\n2. If that authority already exists in the Reference Profile Registry, use **exactly** that profile's `main_title` as the `docid`.\n3. `main_title`, if the authority already exists;\n2. the official or canonical legal title;\n3. a commonly accepted full legal name.\n\n---\n\n# Matching Principles\n\nTwo mentions should receive the **same `docid`** whenever they denote the same underlying legal authority, even if their wording differs.\n\nUse all available evidence, including:\n\n* titles\n* citations\n* abbreviations\n* its `main_title` exactly.\n\nDo **not** generate an alternative wording.\n\n---\n\n## Infer canonical names\n\nIf no matching profile exists, infer the best canonical identifier instead of creating a placeholder.\n\nDo not simply copy the surface form when a more precise legal title is known.\n\n---\n\n## Preserve the original markup\n\nDo not modify the mention.\n\nThe only permitted change is or additional text.\n\n---\n\n# Examples\n\nInput\n\n```xml\n<decision><title>Jordan</title></decision>\n```\n\nOutput\n\n```xml\n<decision docid=\"R. v.
